references.text: The remainder of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons, as most holy among the Lord's fire offerings.
Describes how Aaron and his sons are to eat what remains of the grain offering and confirms that it is most holy.
Explains that the grain offering belongs to the priest who presents it and elaborates on the priests' right to the offerings.
Moses instructs Aaron and his surviving sons to eat the remaining grain offering, for it is most holy.
Confirms that the priests may eat from the most holy things and the holy things.
Describes the priests' portion of the most holy offerings, including the grain offering, which belongs to Aaron and his sons.
Refers to the term 'most holy' (קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים) in connection with the altar.
Expands the rule by specifying that the priest must eat the offering in a holy place.
Confirms and expands the priest's right to most holy offerings to apply to all types of sacrifices.
Confirms that the rule about eating the grain offering is an eternal law for all priestly lines.
Identifies the specific 'anointing portion' due to the priest from the fire offerings.
Specifies that the remainder must be eaten unleavened in a holy place.
